calls.head: There’s no curse: Kochetkov against the Capitals
calls.body: Kochetkov has been shaky against the Capitals since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Hurricanes squeak past the Capitals
paras: Justin Holl made his Capitals debut, after playing for the Blues. Boone Jenner opened the scoring for the Capitals midway through the first. Andrei Svechnikov tied it 1-1 for Carolina early in the second, and the goal stood after the Capitals challenged for goalie interference. The Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall left in the second period and didn’t return. Holl put the Capitals ahead 2-1 early in the period, but they didn’t score again. Eric Robinson tied it 2-2 for Carolina late in the period. Svechnikov scored his second of the night on the power play late in the third to put the Hurricanes ahead for good. Mark Jankowski added the empty-netter with a minute and a half left to make it 4-2. Svechnikov added an assist for a three-point night.

The Hurricanes had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Capitals 35-22. Pyotr Kochetkov made 20 saves for the Canes, and Logan Thompson stopped 31 of 34. The Hurricanes improved to 6-1-1, and the Capitals dropped to 3-3-0.

items.text: The Hurricanes are rolling: six straight wins.
Mark Jankowski has scored in five straight games.
With Jordan Staal out, Jankowski took his spot and scored.
The season series is even at 1-1.
